scope: Android LAN foreground service, lifecycle recovery, logical heartbeat, monotonic timeout/disconnect arbitration, local rule policy vectors

implementation.lifecycleOwner: LanSessionService is a user-started connectedDevice foreground service with a persistent notification; MainActivity only binds and renders snapshots. A partial CPU wake lock is held only while the authority snapshot says the game is ACTIVE and released on terminal state or user stop.
implementation.processDeath: START_NOT_STICKY. The app does not claim OS process survival or automatic host migration. On the next repository creation, one SQLite transaction cancels pending challenges and marks ACTIVE games ABORTED/SYSTEM_ABORT without a winner, retaining already-FINISHED rows.
implementation.heartbeats: Explicit peer heartbeat every 15 seconds from the service while a remote ACTIVE game exists; authenticated snapshot/move/challenge requests also refresh last-seen. Authority detects 30 seconds without a valid participant request and applies a 60-second recovery grace.
implementation.deadlineOrdering: Monotonic deadlines are compared by their original timestamps. The earlier turn timeout or reconnect-grace deadline wins; equal timestamps resolve as TIMEOUT. The disconnected client never authors a result when the authority is unreachable.
implementation.reconnect: NSD same-playerId discovery; token-authenticated snapshot request; apply the host snapshot; only then set sessionReady and enable moves. Saved session identifiers/token allow a process-recreated client to request the same snapshot.
implementation.networkChange: Wi-Fi NetworkCallback rebinds the authority ServerSocket/NSD advertisement after loss, address change, or network handle change. Existing turn deadline is not reset.
